The admin home is `/admin/home`. It shows a header and a grid of widgets.

The header has the date, the title "Dashboard", and a create button. With one content type, the button reads "New `<label>`". With several types, it is a **Create** menu.

## Core widgets

| Widget | Order | Columns | Shows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content-overview` | 0 | 3 | One tile for each content type |
| `content-activity` | 10 | 2 | Items created each week, for the last 12 weeks |
| `quick-actions` | 20 | 1 | Create commands and a few admin destinations |

`content-overview` and `content-activity` are off while no content type is registered.

### Content tiles

Each tile shows the plural label, an icon, and the total. When activity data exists, it adds "+N this week". For a type with a status workflow, it adds a meter of the published share and the text "N published · M drafts". The text says the same numbers, so the share never depends on color alone.

A tile links to the list of the type.

### Activity chart

The chart shows an area for one content type and lines for several. The series colors come from the admin theme.

A hidden table has the same numbers. The chart shows a skeleton while it loads, an error alert with **Try again**, "Activity is not available" when no adapter can count by creation date, and an empty state when nothing was created.

The data comes from this route:

```text
GET /api/_pluto/content-activity/<type>?weeks=12
```

`weeks` is from 1 to 52. The answer is `{ supported, interval: 'week', points: [{ start, count }] }`, oldest first. Weeks start on Monday, in UTC.

The route calls the optional `countCreated(ctx, { from, to })` of the adapter once for each week. It returns `supported: false` when the adapter has no such method, or when the method returns `null`.

### Quick actions

The widget shows the same Create and Go to commands as the [command palette](/core/command-palette), without Home.

## Add a widget

```ts [app/plugins/pluto-registrations.ts]
const RecentPostsWidget = defineAsyncComponent(() => import('../components/RecentPostsWidget.vue'))

export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => {
  definePlutoExtension({
    id: 'supabase-blog',
    dashboardWidgets: [
      { id: 'recent-posts', component: RecentPostsWidget, colSpan: 2 }
    ]
  })
})
```

A widget with the default order (100) goes below the core widgets. The grid has 3 columns on the `lg` breakpoint.

Each widget has its own `<Suspense>`. The grid paints at once. A card skeleton shows until the widget code loads. The skeleton height depends on `colSpan`.

## Translation

All dashboard text is translated. Numbers and dates use `n()` and `d()`, so they follow the admin language.
